key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can use motion time-series to estimate both the state and hydrodynamic coefficients in the Cummins equations for floating offshore structures.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven way to identify added mass, damping, and restoring terms from measured motions, supporting model calibration and design of offshore floating systems.
method: Embed the Cummins equations in a PINN as a first-order dynamical system.
Use observed translational and rotational motion data to estimate the body state.
Solve the inverse problem to infer hydrodynamic coefficients from the learned dynamics.
evidence_signal: The method was verified on free-decay cases for a sphere and a box, and it achieved accurate state and coefficient estimates when sufficient-quality movement data were available.
watch_item: Performance depends on the amount and quality of motion data, so sparse or noisy measurements may reduce coefficient accuracy.
paper_title: Estimating Hydrodynamic Coefficients for Floating Offshore Structures from Movement Data Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
